articles.title: AI for homework—parents more willing to pay subscriptions for their children as peer pressure rises
articles.description: Many parents have mixed feelings about the unrestricted use of artificial intelligence (AI) for schoolwork. They are concerned about the potential impact on their child's ability to learn but also don't want them to be left behind if other young people are using AI.

articles.title: Greenstone Biosciences Receives NIH R61 Grant to Advance Cardiac Fibrosis Therapeutics for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
articles.description: PALO ALTO, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- #BioPharma--Greenstone Biosciences, a biotechnology company advancing New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) for drug discovery, today announced that it has received a Catalyze R61 award from the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), a component of the National Institutes of Health (NIH). articles.title: Bacterial enzyme switch could weaken antibiotic defenses in MRSA and other pathogens
articles.description: If you ask Vijay Parashar, associate professor of medical and molecular sciences (MMSC) at the University of Delaware College of Health Sciences, human bodies are bags of bacteria. "It sounds gross, but not all bacteria are bad; most of them are good. The trouble starts when the bad bacteria learn how to outsmart antibiotics."

articles.title: US nuclear startup achieves first reactor criticality in under one year at Texas site
articles.description: Oklo's Groves reactor reaches first criticality in under a year, advancing its plans for domestic isotope production

articles.title: An elegant modification doubles the range of low-noise 'white lasers' in a single fiber
articles.description: Supercontinuum light sources—often called "white lasers" because they emit a broad, continuous rainbow of colors—are essential tools for everything from advanced medical imaging to environmental gas detection. However, researchers have historically faced a frustrating trade-off: A broad spectrum comes at the expense of high fluctuations, which has effectively limited their use.

articles.title: One-mile underground nuclear reactor wins DOE safety approval for commercial pilot
articles.description: Deep Fission reached a key DOE milestone as its mile-deep Gravity reactor moves toward demonstration at a commercial pilot site in Kansas.

articles.title: Q&A: Mushroom behind 'tiny people' hallucinations identified
articles.description: People in communities thousands of miles apart have described the same strange experience after eating a mysterious mushroom: vivid visions of tiny humans moving through and interacting with the physical world around them. Known as Lilliputian hallucinations—a reference to the 6-inch-tall inhabitants of "Gulliver's Travels"—the phenomenon has long been thought to stem from cultural influences rather than biology.

articles.title: Nothing to fear: AI just created a virus that is not found in nature
articles.description: The results have inspired equal parts hope and terror about the future of AI-inflected biology

articles.title: How 'smart' hydrogel packaging tells you if your food is still fresh
articles.description: The cuts of meat in a supermarket case can look perfectly fresh even as bacteria are already multiplying inside the package. Is there a way to know before you open it?

articles.title: Milky Way-like simulation reveals how central galactic structures grow together
articles.description: Understanding the formation and evolution of the centers of galaxies is one of the most intriguing challenges in astrophysics. The new study aims to unveil the physical processes that led to the formation of two striking features surrounding the black holes at the centers of most galaxies: nuclear star clusters and nuclear stellar disks. Only in the last decade have such galactic structures been observed in the Milky Way and extragalactic systems.

articles.title: With new digital tools, researchers are helping Joshua trees survive wildfires
articles.description: When UC Berkeley postdoctoral researchers Maya Zomer and Lucia Layritz first drove through burned portions of Mojave National Preserve in Southern California, the sight stunned them. "It looks like a pretty dystopian landscape," Layritz said.

articles.title: Mitochondria act as sensors for essential iron molecule, study reveals
articles.description: Heme, a bioactive form of iron, has numerous essential functions in the cell. As a key component of hemoglobin, it enables oxygen transport in the blood. In addition, it performs important functions in other proteins in processes ranging from energy conversion to signal transduction.

articles.title: Fruit and honey fuelled the early evolution of the human brain
articles.description: Intelligence is an energetically expensive luxury. And a new study in Science shows meat has never been the main fuel source for our ancestors.

articles.title: 85% of Australians will complete the census online. Here’s how to avoid potential scams
articles.description: People still remember the 2016 #CensusFail. So how safe is the 2026 census?

articles.title: Two decades of blazar observations, and the mysteries keep piling up
articles.description: Narrow jets of luminous matter may be emitted toward Earth from the nuclei of active galaxies billions of light-years away. The galaxy then appears as a point source and is called a blazar. A Polish-German team of scientists has, for the first time, analyzed the activity of one such blazar over an extended period and, instead of finding answers, encountered an ever-increasing number of intriguing questions.

articles.title: Checking out AI: University library puts emerging technology to the test
articles.description: In a meeting room at the C. V. Starr East Asian Library, a Chinese film poster flickers onto a large screen. Haiqing Lin, the library's head of technical services, is demonstrating an interface he built. With a few practiced clicks, he sends the image—one of 2,000 posters from the Paul Fonoroff collection—through an artificial intelligence model. Seconds later, a draft catalog description appears.

articles.title: STAT+: FDA approves Replimune melanoma drug previously rejected twice
articles.description: The FDA approved Replimune’s treatment for advanced melanoma, dealing the company and patient advocates a big win after a tumultuous saga.

articles.title: Trump Administration to Pay RWE to Cancel Wind Leases
articles.description: It was the fifth such deal struck by the administration to get companies to drop offshore wind projects.

articles.title: With ARPA-H Award, UC San Diego Engineers will Develop a Soft, Autonomous Robot for Stroke Care
articles.description: A research team led by engineers at UC San Diego was awarded up to $26.1M from ARPA-H to develop a soft, flexible robot that can safely and autonomously navigate through the tiny blood vessels of the brain and remove clots, expanding access to a life-saving stroke treatment.

articles.title: Student Creates AI-Powered Tool to Analyze Classroom Space Usage on Charles River Campus
articles.description: A BU student helped design a new optimization and visualization tool to analyze how BU assigns nearly 4,500 classes to hundreds of classrooms each semester.

articles.title: Carbon nanostructure improves fuel-cell catalyst durability while reducing platinum use
articles.description: The explosion of new data centers being proposed and built around the U.S. has increased demand for energy to keep them powered and cooled. The Electric Power Research Institute estimates that data centers could consume up to 9% of U.S. electricity generation annually by 2030, up from 4% of total load in 2023.

articles.title: How evolution fine tunes molecular mechanisms to create and maintain membrane diversity between species
articles.description: The cell membrane is a fundamental biological structure. These lipid layers surround and organize every cell, controlling everything from signaling to transport. But for membranes to function properly, their physicochemical properties must sit within a narrow range: for instance, not too rigid or too fluid.

articles.title: How to See Lunar Rainbows and Petroglyphs While You Travel, Map Ancient Roman Routes, and Safely Leave a Campsite
articles.description: Learn more about the proper ways to clean up a campsite and campfire, and where you can see some amazing natural wonders.

articles.title: New chemical adsorption 10 kW prototype heat pump uses industrial waste heat to provide cooling
articles.description: The new system can drive cooling using waste heat. It combines chemical adsorption with a silent electrochemical compressor, thereby replacing heavy, grid-straining machinery with an almost silent, highly efficient cooling solution.

articles.title: Deworming products for grazing animals may disrupt food chains
articles.description: Researchers from Kiel University and Trier University have shown, for the first time, that a widely used deworming product for grazing animals doesn't just harm individual plants and insects but also alters entire networks of ecological relationships. The active ingredient investigated was moxidectin in the formulation Cydectin, which farmers commonly use against parasites in grazing animals.

articles.title: X(2370) emerges as glueball-dominated particle in collider experiments
articles.description: At the International Conference on High Energy Physics in Brazil, the BESIII Collaboration report that, after 15 years of sustained research, it identified the dominant constituent of the X(2370) as a pseudoscalar glueball with spin-parity quantum numbers of 0−+.

articles.description: BEIJING — In China, robots are being used to inject pigs with vaccines to support intelligent pig farming and meet the production demands of the world’s biggest pork-producing nation.

articles.title: Moovit unveils new function to maximize walking, 'biohacks' based on Bar-Ilan University research
articles.description: A route option inspired by research at Bar-Ilan University aims to help public transportation users increase their daily activity without adding time to their commute.

articles.title: One-wheeled AI security robot could patrol your property
articles.description: The 1Rollo one-wheeled AI security robot uses a spinning flywheel to balance while patrolling properties at speeds up to 19 mph on a single charge.

articles.title: Opinion: One year since Kennedy canceled mRNA vaccine projects, science shows how wrong he was
articles.description: “The United States invented this platform and is the only country walking away from it,” Jeff Coller writes of mRNA vaccines.

articles.title: Songbirds may have developed sharper senses to de-husk seeds
articles.description: Songbirds, birds belonging to the Passeriformes order, are best known for their ability to produce complex musical sounds. Yet some songbird species also have another remarkable skill: They can easily remove the tough layer covering seeds (i.e., the husk) before swallowing their nutritious interiors.

articles.title: Educational psychologists warn of growing pressure on children's services
articles.description: Growing backlogs in Education, Health and Care Needs Assessments (EHCNAs) are making it difficult for educational psychologists to prioritize early intervention because they are weighed down by statutory assessments.

articles.title: 45th St. Jude Runs Crosses $100 Million Milestone
articles.description: MEMPHIS, Tenn.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--St. Jude Runs reached a historic milestone last week of $101 million raised for St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital® since the event’s founding in 1982. More than 200 runners departed from the St. Jude campus in Memphis to complete a 465-mile journey to Peoria, Illinois, where they were joined by participants from 32 community runs across Illinois and Missouri. articles.title: Improving oats for growers and consumers
articles.description: Heart-healthy oats are finding their way into a wider variety of products and recipes as consumer demand grows. Although oats are grown on far fewer acres than other U.S. crops, farmers are able to keep up with demand through genetic gains in yield and other important agronomic traits.

articles.title: New video of Sun’s surface shows swirling plasma patterns in never-before-seen detail
articles.description: New footage of the Sun ’s visible surface shows tiny swirling, vortex-like patterns in never-before-seen detail.

articles.title: Most detailed images taken of sun's surface revealed: "Major step forward"
articles.description: Researchers were able to peek at the sun's scorching surface with the help of the National Science Foundation's Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope​, located on the island of Maui in Hawaii.

articles.title: Archeologists uncover incredible relic from 1854 during Melbourne sewer upgrade
articles.description: Workers in the CBD stopped, so experts could examine the find.

articles.title: Giant mirrors in space to give sun on demand, but project raises concerns
articles.description: It sounds like science fiction – a giant mirror launched into space to illuminate the night sky. But this could be a reality later this year, and it’s raising concerns.

articles.title: Miniaturized laser technology paves the way for fundamental physics experiments in space
articles.description: An international team of researchers has succeeded in producing atomic quantum gas mixtures with an unprecedented particle flux. In the journal Nature Communications, the scientists report on experiments conducted with the MAIUS-B apparatus, in which Bose–Einstein condensates (BECs) consisting of two different atomic species—rubidium and potassium—were generated and studied under microgravity conditions in the Einstein Elevator at Leibniz University Hannover in Germany.

articles.title: One of the world's only two complete dodo skulls reveals new clues about the extinct bird
articles.description: Only two complete dodo skulls are known to exist anywhere in the world: one at the Natural History Museum Denmark and one at the Oxford University Museum of Natural History. The specimen housed in Copenhagen has been preserved in the museum's collections for centuries and has now contributed to an international study led by researchers at the University of Lethbridge in Canada investigating a question that has puzzled researchers for generations: How did the dodo experience the world around it?

articles.title: Technology enables penetration of mineral zone discovered 40 years ago
articles.description: A mining company says it has found a way to access a mineral lode discovered under Broken Hill more than 40 years ago, but once deemed too difficult to reach.

articles.title: Air-stable, ultrathin superconductors developed for more scalable quantum devices
articles.description: Super-thin superconducting materials, which are only one or a few atoms thick, have unique properties scientists can leverage to produce more compact, scalable, and efficient quantum devices. But these fragile materials degrade so rapidly in air that they are difficult to study or manufacture.

articles.title: A Rare Glimpse of a Supernova’s First Light Captured 500 Million Light Years Away
articles.description: Learn more about what the first few moments of a supernova look like and the international collaboration that helped with these findings.

articles.title: Lunar helium-3 eyed as fuel for 50-MWe next-gen US fusion plant planned for 2031
articles.description: TAE Technologies secures a prospective helium-3 fuel option as it advances plans for its first commercial fusion power plant.

articles.title: Long-term study suggests landfill methane emissions are far higher than estimates
articles.description: Methane is an especially potent greenhouse gas, causing much more warming than carbon dioxide on a unit-for-unit basis—and a new, uniquely long-term study of emissions at a New Jersey landfill suggests that estimates of methane pollution in the U.S. and elsewhere may be dramatically off. The study, published by researchers at Columbia University's Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory, which is part of the Columbia Climate School, used continuous ground-based measurements to determine that landfill methane emissions are likely much higher than current estimates.
